name: Seoul
summary: Joseon palaces and hanok lanes, Gwangjang Market's street food, Namsan's tower views, nights out in Hongdae and Myeongdong, and city-wall hikes on Inwangsan and Bukhansan.

months.note: Bitterly cold and dry; good for skiing trips and winter festivals.
Still freezing; Seollal (Lunar New Year, 17 Feb 2026) empties the city as many shops close.
Thawing, with spring yellow dust and fine-dust days.
Cherry blossom peaks in early April (Yeouido, Seokchon Lake), drawing crowds.
Warm, sunny and lively, with Buddha's Birthday lantern festivals.
Getting hot; the jangma monsoon arrives late in the month.
Peak monsoon with heavy downpours and high humidity.
Hot and wet; Korean summer holidays fill beaches more than Seoul.
Clearing skies; Chuseok (around 24–26 Sep 2026) brings travel rushes and palace events.
Crisp and clear with autumn leaves starting; the best weather of the year.
Fall foliage in early November, then quickly colder.
Cold; Christmas lights in Myeongdong and Cheonggyecheon.

tips.title: K-ETA waived through 2026
tips.body: Korea has extended its temporary K-ETA exemption from 1 January to 31 December 2026 for 67 countries and territories, including the US, UK, most of the EU, Canada, Australia, Japan, Singapore and Taiwan. No extension beyond 2026 has been announced, so check your nationality at k-eta.go.kr.

tips.title: e-Arrival Card is mandatory
tips.body: Since 1 January 2026, foreign visitors must submit the free e-Arrival Card at e-arrivalcard.go.kr within 72 hours before arrival and show the QR code at immigration. Paper cards have been discontinued for most visitors. Valid K-ETA holders are exempt.

tips.title: Bukchon Hanok Village curfew
tips.body: In the Bukchon-ro 11-gil 'red zone', tourists are barred from 5pm to 10am, with fines of up to ₩100,000. Residents and hanok-stay guests are exempt. Other lanes are monitored, so keep your voice down.

tips.title: Use Naver Map or KakaoMap
tips.body: Google Maps still lacks full walking and driving directions in Korea, and locals rely on Naver and Kakao. Korea has approved exporting map data to Google under strict conditions, but no date has been set for full navigation.

tips.title: WOWPASS: prepaid card plus T-money
tips.body: WOWPASS is a prepaid card you can use at Korean shops that accept local cards, and it has a built-in T-money transit function. The T-money balance is topped up separately from the WOWPASS balance.

tips.title: One card for subway and bus
tips.body: With WOWPASS's T-money function, or a standalone T-money card, you can tap through subways and buses without buying separate tickets.

tips.title: Skip the e-Arrival Card and you'll queue
tips.body: Travellers who have not filed the e-Arrival Card are sent to self-service kiosks at the airport, which can mean long waits at peak times.

places.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
places.blurb: The largest and main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, with daily gate-guard ceremonies at Gwanghwamun.
places.tip: Free entry if you wear hanbok. Closed Tuesdays.

places.name: Changdeokgung Palace
places.blurb: UNESCO-listed Joseon palace known for its rear Secret Garden (Huwon), visited by guided tour.
places.tip: The Secret Garden is a guided tour for 5,000 KRW more. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Changgyeonggung Palace
places.blurb: Joseon palace adjoining Changdeokgung, with a pond and a Victorian-style glass greenhouse.

places.name: Jongmyo Shrine
places.blurb: UNESCO-listed royal ancestral shrine of the Joseon kings.

places.name: Deoksugung Palace
places.blurb: Compact palace mixing Korean halls and Western-style buildings, beside the Deoksugung stone-wall walk.

places.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
places.blurb: Residential neighborhood of preserved traditional hanok houses between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung.
places.tip: Tourists are barred from the red zone from 5 pm to 10 am, with fines up to 100,000 KRW.

places.name: Insadong
places.blurb: Pedestrian street of galleries, tea houses and traditional craft shops, including the Ssamziegil complex.

places.name: Jogyesa Temple
places.blurb: Head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism and center of the Lotus Lantern Festival.

places.name: Gwanghwamun Square
places.blurb: Central plaza with statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin and an underground exhibition hall.

places.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
places.blurb: Restored 11 km urban stream with walking paths below street level.

places.name: Inwangsan Mountain
places.blurb: Rocky peak traversed by the Seoul City Wall trail with views over the palace district.

places.name: Gwangjang Market
places.blurb: One of Seoul's oldest traditional markets, famed for bindaetteok, mayak gimbap and raw-food stalls.

places.name: Myeongdong
places.blurb: Dense shopping district known for cosmetics stores and evening street-food stalls.

places.name: N Seoul Tower
places.blurb: Communications and observation tower atop Namsan, reachable on foot or by the Namsan cable car.

places.name: Hongdae
places.blurb: Youthful nightlife and busking district around Hongik University.

places.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
places.blurb: Zaha Hadid-designed curving landmark hosting exhibitions, beside the Dongdaemun History & Culture Park.

places.name: Ihwa Mural Village
places.blurb: Hillside residential neighborhood with murals near Naksan Park and the city wall.

places.name: COEX Mall
places.blurb: Large underground mall home to the Starfield Library, near Bongeunsa Temple.

places.name: Common Ground
places.blurb: Shopping and dining complex built from shipping containers.

places.name: Ewha Womans University
places.blurb: University campus known for the sunken ECC building designed by Dominique Perrault.

places.name: Tapgol Park
places.blurb: Small historic park, site of the 1919 March 1st independence declaration reading, with a ten-story stone pagoda.

places.name: Trickeye Museum Seoul
places.blurb: Interactive optical-illusion and AR art museum at 20 Hongik-ro 3-gil.

places.name: Bukhansan National Park
places.blurb: Granite mountain park on Seoul's northern edge whose highest peak is Baegundae (836 m).

places.name: Siloam Sauna
places.blurb: Large 24-hour jjimjilbang near Seoul Station that is popular with foreign travelers.

places.name: Lotte World Tower – Seoul Sky
places.blurb: Observation decks on floors 117–123 of Korea's tallest building, including a glass-floor skydeck.

places.name: Lotte World Adventure
places.blurb: Large indoor theme park with an outdoor Magic Island section and an attached folk museum.

places.name: Nami Island
places.blurb: River island famed for tree-lined avenues, reached by ferry or zipline from Gapyeong.

places.name: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Seoul
places.blurb: National modern and contemporary art museum between Gyeongbokgung and Bukchon.

places.name: Cafe Comma
places.blurb: Multi-floor book cafe run by publisher Munhakdongne.

places.name: DMZ half-day tour
places.blurb: Guided tours from Seoul to the Demilitarized Zone border sites.
places.tip: JSA (Panmunjom) tours have been on and off: check the status before you book.

places.name: Jihwaja
places.blurb: Restaurant serving Joseon royal court cuisine.

places.name: Hanboknam Gyeongbokgung
places.blurb: Hanbok rental shop near Gyeongbokgung Station.

places.name: Chatteul Tea House
places.blurb: Traditional hanok tea house serving tea and rice cakes.

places.name: Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha street
places.blurb: Strip of evening tented street stalls serving snacks and soju.

places.name: Guerlain Spa, The Shilla Seoul
places.blurb: Luxury hotel spa inside The Shilla Seoul.

places.name: Butterfinger Pancakes
places.blurb: American-style all-day breakfast chain.

places.name: Apgujeong Rodeo Street
places.blurb: Upscale fashion and boutique district.

places.name: Four Seasons Hotel Seoul
places.blurb: Luxury hotel steps from Gwanghwamun Square.

places.name: Holiday Inn Express Seoul Hongdae
places.blurb: Midrange IHG hotel beside Hongik University Station.
